issue.title: ImportError on master: project_handler.py imports project_accent_map, privatized to _project_accent_map by a3765f857
issue.description:
`import sase.main.project_handler` raises ImportError on master (daa095ec3), so
`just check` fails at `lint (mypy)` and any code path that imports the project
handler dies at import time.

Commit a3765f857 ("fix(lint): drop stale symvision epic-symbol entry and privatize
project_accent_map") renamed `project_accent_map` to `_project_accent_map` in
`src/sase/ace/tui/project_styles.py` on the stated grounds that it "has no non-test
caller outside its own file". That premise is wrong: `src/sase/main/project_handler.py`
imports it at line 16 and calls it at line 599. That commit changed only
`src/sase/ace/tui/project_styles.py` and `tests/ace/tui/test_project_styles.py`, so the
caller was left pointing at a name that no longer exists.

Found while splitting `tests/test_vcs_xprompt_mru.py` into per-concern modules
(tests-only diff); reproduced with all local changes limited to `tests/`.

Repro on master daa095ec3 in workspace sase_13:

    just install
    .venv/bin/python -c "import sase.main.project_handler"
    # ImportError: cannot import name 'project_accent_map' from
    # 'sase.ace.tui.project_styles' (src/sase/ace/tui/project_styles.py)

    just check
    # .venv/bin/mypy
    # src/sase/main/project_handler.py:16: error: Module
    #   "sase.ace.tui.project_styles" has no attribute "project_accent_map";
    #   maybe "_project_accent_map", "project_accent", or
    #   "_project_accent_map_cached"?  [attr-defined]
    # Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 3469 source files)
    # error: recipe `_lint-mypy` failed

Likely fix: `project_accent_map` does have a real external caller, so restore the public
name (and its `__all__`/test references) rather than re-privatizing; symvision's
unused-public-symbol rule should not have fired for it in the first place. Whoever works
this should double-check why the symvision scan did not see the `project_handler.py`
caller, since a wrong "no external caller" verdict is the underlying hazard.

task_type_fields.impact: Every agent's just check goes red at the mypy gate on master, and sase.main.project_handler is unimportable at runtime, so any CLI path that touches the project handler raises ImportError.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-q5 — same symvision unused-public-symbol pass that motivated a3765f857; that bead's description cites the stale sase-pw.8(project_accent_map) --epic-symbol entry whose removal exposed this symbol to the scan. Anyone fixing q5 should not repeat the privatize-without-checking-callers move that produced this ImportError.

RELATED: sase-lg (closed) — identical failure shape: a symvision-driven privatization (stream_and_parse_messages_json_output) left an in-tree importer behind and broke master with an ImportError. Its fix is the precedent for this one.
